# Compiler Pipeline

This reference describes the compiler pipeline.
The pipeline uses explicit Rust product types between major stages.

## Build Data Flow

The main project build follows this sequence:

```text
command arguments
  -> manifest validation and artifact selection
  -> source graph discovery
  -> per-file loading and parsing
  -> top-level compile-time selection and normalization
  -> generic and statement instantiation
  -> layout semantic checking for a final-link artifact
  -> source semantic checking, with selected layout facts when present
  -> semantic module interface generation
  -> provisional typed IR construction and verification when #eval is present
  -> deterministic #eval execution, constant injection, and final IR verification when required
  -> artifact reachability
  -> concrete type layout
  -> callable ABI classification
  -> AArch64 machine lowering
  -> per-module ET_REL native objects
  -> static archive assembly or final placement and ELF linking
  -> artifact output
```

The compiler validates the manifest before it selects an artifact plan.
The plan identifies the source graph, target, layout, policies, and outputs.

The compiler loads each source file separately.
Each parsed file retains its file identity and local spans.
A mapped source joins these files for diagnostics and reports.
The frontend does not reparse mapped source as one source file.

Normalization performs top-level compile-time selection and source-shape normalization.
Instantiation expands concrete generics and compile-time statements.
Semantic checking consumes only the instantiated tree.

Before concrete generic expansion, the compiler authenticates each generic body
against its built-in or static-interface constraints. During expansion, a
concrete subject selects its unique static-interface implementation and every
interface-qualified call becomes an ordinary direct call. No unresolved static
interface call reaches ordinary semantic checking or typed IR.

The compiler checks the selected final-link layout before it checks source with layout facts.
A static-library build checks source without a final-link layout.
The checked source keeps its instantiated tree and semantic facts together.
The checked layout keeps its tree, semantic facts, and layout facts together.

IR construction consumes these checked products.
IR verification checks structural rules and memory-safety facts.
When the source contains `#eval`, the compiler verifies provisional IR, runs
each eligible target through reference execution, injects the results, and
verifies final IR. Provisional proof products do not enter the final artifact.
The artifact path then retains reachable declarations.

The backend computes concrete type layouts and callable ABI facts.
It then performs register allocation and AArch64 instruction lowering.
Native-object emission creates one `ET_REL` product for each selected module product.

A static-library build creates an archive and its semantic-module-interface companion.
A final-link build performs placement and integrated ELF linking.
These paths do not invoke an external linker or archive tool.

## Check Data Flow

`wync check` uses the manifest, source graph, normalization, and semantic-checking stages.
It also creates semantic module interfaces in memory.

The checker creates verified IR when indexing requires a memory-safety proof or
when a source contains `#eval`.
It does not enter type layout, ABI, machine lowering, object emission, or final assembly.
See [Check, Format, and Diagnostics](check-format-and-diagnostics.md).

## Report Data Flow

Storage and layout reports stop after the checked frontend.
Effects reports consume verified typed IR and semantic effect facts.
Lowering and resources reports also consume ABI, machine code, and native artifacts.
Reference execution consumes verified typed IR and scenario state.

Report data does not flow back into compilation.
See [Compiler Inspection Reports](inspection-reports.md).

## Build Sessions And Cache

One build uses one in-memory `BuildSession`.
The session can reuse typed products with identical semantic fingerprints.
The session records dependencies and timing observations for that process.

Artifact builds can also reuse semantic-module-interface and native-object pairs across processes.
The compiler uses this cache only when the host path passes its safety checks.
A cache miss does not change program acceptance or generated bytes.

The default cache byte limit is 1,073,741,824 bytes.
Set `WYNC_CACHE_MAX_BYTES=0` to disable persistent reuse.
Set `WYNC_CACHE_DIR` to select a different cache root.

On macOS, the default root is `~/Library/Caches/wync`.
On other Unix hosts, the root is `$XDG_CACHE_HOME/wync` or `~/.cache/wync`.

## Resource Limits

The compiler rejects one source file larger than 8,388,608 bytes.
The parser permits at most 64 active nesting levels.

Generic materialization has these limits per module:

- 1,024 concrete instantiations;
- 64 active instantiation trace entries;
- 64 nested generic type nodes; and
- 4,096 bytes in one generated symbol name.

A zero-padded fixed `[N]u8` string initializer has a 1,048,576-byte materialization limit.
A fixed-array repeat literal has a 1,048,576-element expansion limit.
Checked assembly and ELF alignment values cannot exceed 1,048,576 bytes.

One statically linked ELF artifact cannot exceed 67,108,864 bytes.
The same limit applies to intermediate text layouts for that artifact.
The ELF writer supports at most 65,279 sections.

## Failure And Diagnostics

Each stage returns a typed product or a diagnostic.
A failed stage does not run a later artifact stage.

The detecting stage selects the diagnostic kind and occurrence details.
Text, JSON, and LSP renderers do not change the acceptance result.
